title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is the base level of Grothendieck's Teichmüller tower: U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,∞}, seen as the Riemann sphere Σ. The real circle is the 'equator'. The two hemisphere centres P_+ and P_- (written P_ε) are the points (1 ± i√3)/2, which are the fixed points of the order-3 rotation. On the equator there are auxiliary points Q_i. Since the reflection σ̃_∞ fixes ∞ and Q_∞, Q_∞ is presumably 1/2, the midpoint of the arc 0–1 not containing ∞.

A 'repère' (frame) is r = (i, ω, ϖ):
- i ∈ {0,1,∞} is a marked point;
- ω = ±1 is a cyclic orientation of the three points along the equator, and ωi denotes the next point;
- ϖ = ±1 is an orientation of the sphere;
- ε = ω∧ϖ picks out the hemisphere P_ε.

The extended symmetry group Γ = S_3 × {1,τ}, with τ complex conjugation, has order 12 and acts simply transitively on the 12 repères. For a repère r, u_r ∈ Γ is the unique element sending the standard repère (∞,+1,+1) to r, and in particular sending P_+ to P_ε. Then ψ_r = π_1(u_r) : Π_{0,3} = π_1(U_{0,3},P_+) → Π_ε = π_1(U_{0,3},P_ε). These are the isomorphisms used to attach copies of Π_{0,3} at the various base points; the previous page (diagram 37) shows they are compatible with transport of structure.

The stabilizer of P_+ is S̃_3 = Γ_{P_+} = {(g, τ^α) : α = 0 if g is even, α = 1 if g is odd}. It is isomorphic to S_3 and consists of:
- the rotations by ±1/3 turn about the P_+P_- axis (holomorphic);
- the three anti-holomorphic reflections σ̃_i in the meridian great circles through i and Q_i. For example, σ̃_∞ : z ↦ 1 - z̄ swaps 0 and 1 and fixes ∞.

This page:
1. Any repère r' with the same ε is r' = r g_0 with g_0 ∈ S̃_3, i.e. u_{r'} = u_r u_{g_0} (38).
2. Because g_0 fixes P_+, functoriality of π_1 gives ψ_{r'} = ψ_r ∘ π_1(g_0, P_+), a genuine automorphism of Π_{0,3}, not just an outer one.
3. Made explicit for the generators:
   - g_0 = ρ (one-third turn): rρ = (ωi, ω, ϖ), so ψ_ε^{ωi,ω} = ψ_ε^{i,ω} ∘ ρ. Here ρ is also viewed as an automorphism of Π_{0,3}, induced by the rotation about P_±, which shifts the marked point along the ω-orientation of the equator.
   - g_0 = σ̃_∞ (orientation-reversing: 0↔1, ∞ fixed): rσ̃_∞ = (i, ω', ϖ') with ω' = -ω and ϖ' = -ϖ, so ε is unchanged and ψ_ε^{i,ω'} = ψ_ε^{i,ω} ∘ σ̃_∞ (41).

The marginal figure shows the triangle of base points P_ε, R_{ωi} = R_1 and R_{ωi} = R_0, joined by paths l_0 and ω' and passing near Q_∞. These are the 'flags marqués' and paths used in the isomorphisms (39).

Purpose: to reduce the full system of gluing isomorphisms indexed by 12 frames to a few explicit automorphisms of Π_{0,3} induced by the hemisphere-preserving symmetry group. The next page does the same for the equatorial base points Q_i, whose stabilizer is Z/2 × Z/2 generated by σ_∞ and τ. This is groundwork for writing the action of Γ, and ultimately of Gal(Q̄/Q), on the gluing data of the Teichmüller tower in Π_{0,3}.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The computation rσ̃_∞ = (i, -ω, -ϖ) is consistent: Grothendieck crossed out an 'ω' in front of i, correctly keeping i fixed. The ρ formula's direction convention (rρ = (ωi, ω, ϖ)) depends on the unstated convention for which rotation ρ is; this is fine but implicit.

The identification of ρ and σ̃_∞ with automorphisms of Π_{0,3} (rather than outer automorphisms) is legitimate only because they fix the base point P_+. The page states this implicitly ('π_1(g_0, P_+)'), not explicitly. Concrete formulas for these automorphisms in terms of generators are not yet given ('expliciter ceci').

ideas.what: Frames (repères) (i, ω, ϖ) on the tripod sphere, on which the extended symmetry group S_3 × Z/2 (with complex conjugation) acts simply transitively; the gluing isomorphisms ψ_r are indexed by frames.
ideas.modern_name: Symmetries of P^1-{0,1,∞} including complex conjugation; torsor of 'markings'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Ihara, Drinfeld (1990) and Lochak–Schneps work on GT; Grothendieck's Esquisse (1984) for the Lego viewpoint
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the base level P^1-{0,1,∞} and its symmetries qualitatively; this bookkeeping is not published

ideas.what: Using the hemisphere centres P_± (fixed points of the order-3 rotation, (1±i√3)/2) as base points, so that the stabilizer S̃_3 (rotations plus anti-holomorphic reflections) acts by genuine automorphisms of π_1.
ideas.modern_name: Symmetric base points / fixed points of the S_3 action; anti-holomorphic symmetries acting on π_1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Various authors on GT and the hexagon relation (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura)

ideas.what: Transformation law ψ_{rg_0} = ψ_r ∘ π_1(g_0, P_+), made explicit for g_0 = ρ and g_0 = σ̃_∞ (formulas (38), (41)).
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of π_1 / change of marking

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping of how the 12-element symmetry group of the tripod (with complex conjugation) changes the frame-indexed isomorphisms between fundamental groups at symmetric base points. It is useful groundwork for the Teichmüller-tower/GT programme, but nothing here goes beyond functoriality, and the explicit automorphisms are not yet written down.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the overlined insertion seems to read 'ayant même ε pour' / 'à ε près' and the continuation 'sera de la forme' (not 'serv. ... fig-marquée'); the sense is 'every repère r' with the same ε will be of the form r' = r g_0'.
'(avec u_r(g_0) = g mais peu important)': likely 'pas important'.

The marginal note refers to the isomorphisms '(39)', while the displayed equation on the page is labelled (38). The formula ψ_{r'} = ψ_r ∘ π_1(g_0, P_+) is unnumbered on the page; the marginal note calls these ψ_r, ψ_{r'} 'les isom. (39)'.
In rσ̃_∞ = (i, ω', ϖ') the crossed-out symbol before i is deleted, so i is unchanged. Likewise in (41) the superscript is ψ_ε^{i,ω'}.
The final parenthesis reads roughly '(σ̃_i est la symétrie p.r. aux grands cercles méridiens passant par Q_i)', i.e. the reflection in the meridian great circle through Q_i (and i, P_±).
'où on a identifié ρ aussi à un élément de ...': the object is written with a tilde (possibly Π̃_{0,3}, or meaning Aut(Π_{0,3})). The intended sense is an automorphism of Π_{0,3}.
